arguments.summary: A credential stuffing attack was detected originating from internal host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), masquerading as source IP 10.0.5.14. The attack targeted domain controller 10.0.8.200 with repeated Kerberos TGT request failures (Event ID 4768). Further investigation revealed that the host was compromised via a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, leading to Cobalt Strike beaconing (ET TROJAN signature) to C2 server 198.51.100.23:443. Lateral movement was attempted via SMB to 10.0.5.50. Despite automated containment attempts, credential revocation and endpoint isolation failed due to access restrictions. The host remains a critical risk for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
conditions:
  - Image|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
  - ParentImage|endswith: '\\outlook.exe'
  - CommandLine|contains_any:
    - '-enc'
    - 'Base64'
    - 'IEX'
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
description: Detects encoded PowerShell launched directly from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike Beacon configuration in memory or dump"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $xormagic = { 0x41 0x42 0x43 0x44 } // Example XOR key pattern
        $cfg = "windows/beacon" wide ascii
    condition:
        $xormagic at 0 and $cfg
}
